keyVerseText: And Zorobabel begat Abiud; and Abiud begat Eliakim; and Eliakim begat Azor;
rootMeaning: The name Ἀβιούδ (Abioúd) originates from the Hebrew אֲבִיהוּד (ʼĂbîyhûwd), meaning 'my father is majesty.' This etymology highlights a profound acknowledgment of divine sovereignty and honor attributed to God as a father figure. Beyond the simple transliteration 'Abiud,' the root sense conveys a personal and reverent connection to God's majestic character, enriching the understanding of the name within the biblical narrative.
usageInScripture: The word Ἀβιούδ appears only twice in Scripture, both times translated consistently as 'Abiud.' Its limited occurrence, specifically in Matthew 1:13, situates it within a genealogical context, underscoring the importance of lineage in biblical history. The consistent translation and restricted usage emphasize its role as a proper name rather than a common noun, preserving its identity as an Israelite ancestor.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding the original meaning of Ἀβιούδ as 'my father is majesty' enriches the Christian faith by reminding believers of God's sovereign and majestic nature as a paternal figure. This name within the genealogy of Christ connects the human ancestry of Jesus to a divine reality, affirming God's majestic authority throughout salvation history. It also encourages believers to trust in God's majestic fatherhood as foundational to their identity and faith. The preservation of this name in Scripture highlights God's faithfulness to His covenant people across generations.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 1:13 states, 'And Zorobabel begat Abiud; and Abiud begat Eliakim; and Eliakim begat Azor,' situating Abiud within the direct lineage leading to Christ. The presence of the name Abiud, meaning 'my father is majesty,' in this genealogical record underscores the majestic and divine providence guiding the ancestry of Jesus. It reminds readers that behind these human names stands the majestic Father orchestrating the fulfillment of His redemptive plan.
